cohort: The study included 80 patients who underwent emergency peripartum hysterectomy at a tertiary care hospital between June 2010 and June 2020.
finding: Emergency peripartum hysterectomy (EPH) is a critical procedure for managing life-threatening obstetric hemorrhages, with uterine atony, uterine rupture, and abnormal placentation being the leading indications; a high EPH rate may also be associated with advanced maternal age and high parity.
mod_finding: Among the patients who underwent EPH, 50 cases occurred after cesarean sections and 30 cases followed vaginal deliveries.
